solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Relaxed having lowered pulse

parts.note: something lowered has been brought down
a pulse is a beat, as of the heart

explanation.surface: Someone calm enough that their heart rate has dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A downbeat manner is low-key and casual, so the word can mean relaxed or understated.

clue.text: Escape into valley and remove unwanted coat

indicators.note: the escape letters go into the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley, as in the Yorkshire Dales
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Fleeing into a valley and shedding a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Descaling a kettle or pipe strips off the crust of limescale that has built up.

clue.text: Bank and Temple man held inside before

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia

indicators.note: the man's name is kept within the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
Sid is a man's name

explanation.surface: A bank and a man from the Temple detained earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temple man' reads as one unit, a barrister from London's Inner or Middle Temple, but it splits in two: a Thai temple, then a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of a river or lake is the waterside, the land along the water's edge.

clue.text: Stolen meat comes to philosopher

parts.note: bent is slang for stolen or dishonest
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A philosopher ends up with stolen meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Bentham was the English philosopher who founded utilitarianism.

clue.text: Goddess, second one, encountered sun god rising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
met means encountered
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A goddess meets the sun god at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns SIMETRA upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of hunting and the moon, twin of Apollo.

clue.text: Escort vessel taking line through ducks

parts.note: a gig is a light rowing boat, so a vessel

indicators.note: the line letter is run through the middle of the pair of ducks, so it sits between them

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing, O, so two ducks give OO

explanation.surface: A boat escorting another, its towline threaded past some waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escort' looks like a verb about shipping; it is the noun, a paid companion. In cricket a duck is a nought, so ducks give two O's.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to act as a woman's escort or companion.

clue.text: Something fruity from novelist gone into by censor

indicators.note: the censor word enters the novelist's name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
to gag is to censor or silence

explanation.surface: A racy passage from a novel that the censor has cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a green variety of plum, a fruit.

clue.text: Indian state holds new star losing head in cabin

indicators.note: the state's name holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast

indicators.note: the star word drops its first letter

parts.note: a star is an idol

explanation.surface: An Indian state houses a fading new celebrity in a cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' drops I from IDOL, leaving DOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is the passenger cabin hung from a cable car or an airship.

clue.text: Girl having endless success getting in with US lawyer

indicators.note: the success word loses its last letter

parts.note: luck is success, good fortune
a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A girl's run of success ends with an American attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucinda is a girl's name.

clue.text: Schedule this month one absolutely fixed

parts.note: to schedule a meeting is to set it
inst., short for instant, means this month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A diary entry booked for this month that cannot be moved.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) is an old commercial abbreviation for 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set in stone is permanent and unalterable, like an inscription carved in rock.

clue.text: Cut force at work here

definitions.meaning: to make a small cut in it
in British slang the ... is a police station, where the police force works

explanation.surface: A cut made by something forceful at a workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' is the police; 'the nick' is British slang for a police station (and for prison).
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut, and also slang for the police station where officers are based.

clue.text: One great shot in the box by American player

definitions.text: One great shot in the box by American player

parts.words: One great shot in the box by American player
parts.note: a great man shot while sitting in a theatre box by an actor, an American player

explanation.surface: A fine shot into the penalty box from an American footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads: the president was shot in his box at Ford's Theatre by the actor John Wilkes Booth.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth US president was assassinated in a theatre box by an actor in 1865.

clue.text: Recalled trap set in identical puzzles

indicators.note: something called back is brought back the way it came, so the whole build is read in reverse
the trap word is placed inside the word for identical

parts.note: identical means the same
a gin is a trap for catching game

explanation.surface: A trap, remembered, laid among matching puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' applies to the whole container, so the finished SAMGINE is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmas are riddles or mysteries, things that baffle like puzzles.

clue.text: Champion making an essential point about game

parts.note: taken as written
polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the essential point

explanation.surface: A winner explains the key point of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is a verb-like noun here: one who champions a cause, not a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist defends or argues for a cause, so champions it.

clue.text: Vehicle on the move delivers seed

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
someone away is gone, on the move from home

explanation.surface: A travelling van delivering seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Caraway is a plant whose aromatic seeds flavour bread and cakes.

clue.text: Very slight force fluctuating in the raw outside

indicators.note: something fluctuating keeps changing, so these letters shift into a new order

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wavering force outside in the cold elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluctuating' scrambles F with IN THE RAW; 'outside' completes the outdoor picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Wafer-thin means extremely thin, like a wafer biscuit, so very slight or narrow.

clue.text: Exemption from having to cross ebbing river

indicators.note: the word from spans the river word, straddling it on both sides

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an ebbing tide flows back, so the river's name runs backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Being let off having to ford a retreating river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exemption from' looks like the whole definition, but 'from' is the outer piece; 'ebbing' gives EED.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom from a duty is exemption from it, being released or excused.

clue.text: Irish channel securing opera about to broadcast

indicators.note: the channel's letters secure, enclosing, the opera

parts.note: RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the opera title is reversed

parts.note: Aida is an opera by Verdi

explanation.surface: An Irish TV station gets the rights to an opera to air.
explanation.walkthrough: RTE (Raidió Teilifís Éireann) is Ireland's state broadcaster; 'about' gives ADIA.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to send out in all directions, as a broadcast does.

clue.text: Bound to suffer defeat after short dash around

indicators.note: the defeat word is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: an en dash is the shorter typographic dash
C, for circa, means around
to lose is to suffer defeat

explanation.surface: Bound to lose after a quick sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to'; it is a verb meaning fence in. An en dash is the shorter printed dash.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound an area is to mark its limits, to enclose it.

clue.text: Plump female kindly news boss engages

indicators.note: to engage someone is to take them in, so the pair of words takes the female letter inside

parts.note: to take something well is to take it kindly
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A kindly editor hires a rather plump woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-fed is well nourished, so chubby or plump.

clue.text: Well-heeled wife in the pink having lost first husband

indicators.note: the first letter of the health word is dropped

parts.note: to be in the pink is to be in good health

explanation.surface: A rich wife in good health has shed her first husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having lost first' removes H, the husband, from the front of HEALTHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled is an idiom for rich, as someone with good shoes is prosperous.

clue.text: Moonstruck in a cult after processing

indicators.note: processed material is changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Members of a cult driven mad after being indoctrinated.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic comes from luna, the moon, once believed to cause madness, so moonstruck.

clue.text: Makes casual visit to bishop restricted by medical condition

indicators.note: the bishop is confined within the condition word

parts.note: dropsy is an old name for oedema, fluid swelling
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: Visiting an ailing bishop who is housebound by illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop by is to call in on someone informally, without arranging it.

clue.text: Surgeon (RN) abroad worked for homely philanthropist

parts.note: a surgeon is a kind of doctor

indicators.note: the letters are worked over, kneaded into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A navy surgeon serving overseas on behalf of a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surgeon' tempts toward the heart surgeon Christiaan Barnard, but it gives DOCTOR; 'worked' shuffles RN ABROAD into BARNARDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Barnardo founded children's homes in Victorian London, so he is the philanthropist of homes.

clue.text: Panel gives old man nothing

parts.note: 'old man' is slang for father, dad
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A jury hears that a father contributes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower panelled section of an interior wall.

clue.text: Laughing uncontrollably following theatre visit?

definitions.meaning: after an operating theatre a patient may be literally ..., sewn up

explanation.surface: Helpless with laughter after an evening at a comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre, not a playhouse; the question mark marks the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means laughing so hard it hurts, like a stitch in the side; literally, sutured after surgery.

clue.text: Feel genuinely sorry about gym's charge

indicators.note: the charge word goes round, about, the gym letters

parts.note: rent is a charge for using property
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: Regretting the cost of a gym membership.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel true remorse for a wrong and resolve to change.

clue.text: One's found stunning spot — at city's limits?

parts.note: to spot something is to eye it
the outer letters of the word city are C and Y, read as the phrase C AND Y

explanation.surface: Someone finds a striking place on the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The limits of 'city' are C and Y, which written out in full become C AND Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is a person or thing that is visually attractive but superficial.
